data.title: PeraMorphIQ Unveiled at the Faculty of Engineering 75th Anniversary Exhibition
data.brief: The Department of Computer Engineering at the University of Peradeniya introduced PeraMorphIQ, a new neuromorphic research initiative, during the 75th Anniversary Exhibition, marking the department’s first public showcase of brain-inspired computing research
data.Author: PeraMorphIQ Neuromorphic Research Group
data.fullContent:
As part of the 75th Anniversary Exhibition of the Faculty of Engineering, the Department of Computer Engineering proudly presented its latest advancements in computer architecture, embedded systems, and FPGA-based prototypes. The exhibition highlighted the department’s strong expertise in hardware design and real-time computing, while also unveiling an exciting new frontier for our research community — neuromorphic computing. Through the Embedded Systems and Computer Architecture Lab (ESCAL), our teams demonstrated how we are advancing beyond traditional architectures toward cognitive and brain-inspired systems that integrate intelligence, adaptability, and energy efficiency.
 The event also marked the official introduction of PeraMorphIQ, the department’s dedicated neuromorphic research group. This initiative represents a milestone in the department’s history as the first public showcase of neuromorphic computing. PeraMorphIQ aims to design energy-efficient, brain-inspired architectures, explore Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) as next-generation AI models, and pioneer on-chip learning and memory-optimized systems. The exhibition served as both a celebration of past achievements and a vision for the future, as the department continues to expand collaborations, strengthen its research ecosystem, and position ESCAL and PeraMorphIQ as hubs for cutting-edge computer architecture and neuromorphic innovation.
